unit.label: At the shop
unit.title: Buying Snacks & Asking for Help
unit.description: 10 new words and forms. Ask a shopkeeper a question, order buns, ask for help, and read prices in hundreds and thousands.

goal.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ mǎi liǎng ge bāozi.
goal.meaning: Please buy two buns for me.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 4 請問一共多少錢？ · pp. 66–72, 77, 80.

steps.prompt: Which politely starts a question?
steps.explanation: 請問 opens a question; 謝謝 thanks someone and 好的 acknowledges.
闆 is bǎn: boss; owner (in 老闆).

steps.prompt: Review: a large hot coffee to go is…
steps.explanation: 大杯 = large; 熱咖啡 = hot coffee; 外帶 = to go.

steps.prompt: Review: which asks for the whole order’s price?
steps.explanation: 一共 totals the order.

lessons.title: Order Some Buns
lessons.subtitle: Count filled steamed buns with 個.

steps.prompt: Choose an order for two buns.
steps.explanation: 個 counts buns; use 兩 before 個 for two.
包 is bāo: first syllable of 包子, a filled steamed bun.

steps.prompt: In 包子, how is 子 pronounced?
steps.explanation: The character has dictionary zǐ, but 包子 is bāozi.

steps.prompt: Review: how many is 七十五?
steps.explanation: 七十 is seventy, plus 五.

lessons.title: Ask Someone to Help
lessons.subtitle: Name who the action is for.

steps.prompt: In 請幫她買茶, who is the tea for?
steps.explanation: 她 immediately after 幫 names the beneficiary.

steps.prompt: Which means “He does not buy tea for me”?
steps.explanation: Put the negative before 幫 for this meaning.

steps.prompt: Which pronunciation is used for 微波 here?
steps.explanation: In the Taiwan Mandarin taught here, 微 has second-tone wéi in 微波.

steps.prompt: Review: which politely offers someone tea?
steps.explanation: 請 + action makes the invitation polite.

lessons.title: Prices over One Hundred
lessons.subtitle: Understand the hundreds place and zero.

steps.prompt: Which full number is 105?
steps.explanation: 零 marks the missing tens position.

steps.prompt: Which full number is 110?
steps.explanation: A hundred plus one ten is 一百一十.

steps.prompt: What does 兩百零八 mean?
steps.explanation: 兩百 is 200; 零 marks the missing tens; 八 adds eight.

steps.prompt: Practice menu: coffee costs 80 and two buns cost 50. What is the total?
Review: which number is 48?
steps.explanation: Four tens and eight ones.

lessons.title: Thousands and Ten Thousands
lessons.subtitle: Read larger prices by place value.

steps.prompt: 一萬三千塊 is…
steps.explanation: One ten-thousand plus three thousands = 13,000.

steps.prompt: Which full number is 1,005?
steps.explanation: A single 零 bridges the missing hundreds and tens.

steps.prompt: Which full number is 1,050?
steps.explanation: After the missing hundreds place, 五十 supplies five tens.
萬 is wàn: ten thousand.

steps.prompt: Review: how do you say two cups?
steps.explanation: 兩 counts two before 杯.

steps.prompt: The customer pays for buns. Which action is the customer doing?
steps.explanation: The customer buys, 買 mǎi; the seller sells, 賣 mài.
賣 is mài: sell.

steps.prompt: For that order, which total follows the practice menu?
steps.explanation: Two buns at 25 plus coffee at 80: 25 + 25 + 80 = 130.

steps.prompt: Review: the owner acknowledges your request. Which means OK?
steps.explanation: 好的 acknowledges a request.

lessons.title: Snack Shop Challenge
lessons.subtitle: Handle an order and interpret the price.

steps.prompt: Start a polite price question to the owner.
options: 老闆，請問這杯茶多少錢？
steps.answer: 老闆，請問這杯茶多少錢？
steps.explanation: 老闆 addresses the owner; 請問 opens the price question.

steps.prompt: Ask to have this bun microwaved for you.
steps.explanation: 微波 gives the action; 幫我 means for me.

steps.prompt: Which pronunciation is used for 微波 here?
steps.explanation: In the Taiwan Mandarin taught here, 微 has second-tone wéi in 微波.

steps.prompt: A full price reads 一百零五塊. How much?
steps.explanation: 零 marks the missing tens.

steps.prompt: Read the full number 3,500.
steps.explanation: Three thousands plus five hundreds.

steps.prompt: A seller says 我們賣茶. What do they mean?
steps.explanation: 賣 mài is sell.

steps.prompt: Practice menu: three buns at 25 each and one coffee at 80. Total?
Review: 外帶 or 內用—which means to go?
steps.explanation: 外帶 means taking the order away.

steps.prompt: Review: 你要幾杯茶 asks…
options: How many cups of tea you want
steps.answer: How many cups of tea you want
steps.explanation: 幾杯 asks the cup count.

newVocabulary.note: 子 is neutral-tone zi in this word; the standalone character is zǐ.

newVocabulary.meaning: for; on behalf of (before a person)

newVocabulary.note: Use second-tone wéi in 微波.

闆.note: 闆 completes 老闆, a shop owner or boss. The spoken word has two third tones; keep the dictionary spelling lǎobǎn.
闆.memory: Three small mouths sit inside the 門 frame. Keep space between all three boxes.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: outer door frame
parts.description: The eight-stroke 門 encloses the inside on the top and both sides.

parts.label: 品
parts.name: three inner mouths
parts.description: Write the upper 口, then the lower left and lower right 口 inside the frame.

問.note: In 請問, 問 introduces a question politely.
問.memory: Picture 口 inside 門: a small mouth enclosed by a tall doorway.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door frame
parts.description: 門 makes the outer frame and stays open at the bottom.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth inside
parts.description: 口 is the small three-stroke box inside the lower part of 門.

包.meaning: first syllable of 包子, a filled steamed bun
包.note: 包 begins 包子. Learn the food name as a whole word; this card is not teaching a separate order for a bag.
包.memory: The curved outer 勹 wraps around the small 巳 shape, like a wrapper around a filling.

parts.label: 勹
parts.name: outer wrapping shape
parts.description: Begin with a short left-falling stroke and the long bent hook around the top and right.

parts.label: 巳
parts.name: inner curled shape
parts.description: The three inner strokes make 巳, finishing with the curved stroke at the bottom.

子.note: The dictionary reading is zǐ. In 包子 the suffix is neutral-tone zi: bāozi.
子.memory: 子 has a bent top, a central hooked stroke, and a horizontal stroke through the middle.

parts.label: 子
parts.name: three-stroke 子
parts.description: Write the bent top, central hooked stroke, then the horizontal crossing through it.

幫.meaning: for; on behalf of (in 幫我…)
幫.note: In 請幫我買茶, 幫 introduces the person benefiting from the action: please buy tea for me.
幫.memory: 封 sits above 帛. Keep the lower white box and hanging cloth shape centered under the wide top.

parts.label: 封
parts.name: upper component
parts.description: Write the upper 封 structure, with its stacked 土 shapes and 寸 on the right.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: middle box
parts.description: Write 白 beneath the top, including the short slant above its box.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: lower cloth shape
parts.description: Finish with 巾 below 白; the central vertical extends downward.

微.meaning: first syllable of 微波, to microwave
微.note: Use second-tone wéi in 微波 wéibō.
微.memory: A narrow 彳 stands left of a mountain-and-legs middle; the four-stroke 攵 finishes at the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: left stepping component
parts.description: Two short slants and a vertical make the narrow left component.

parts.label: 山兀
parts.name: middle structure
parts.description: Write the three-stroke 山, the horizontal below it, then the two lower leg strokes.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Finish the right side with a short slant, horizontal, longer left-falling stroke and right-falling stroke.

波.note: 波 means wave; 微波 literally refers to microwaves and is used as the verb to microwave here.
波.memory: The three water strokes 氵 are on the left, with 皮 on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: Place the three water strokes down the left, with the last one rising.

parts.label: 皮
parts.name: right component
parts.description: In the Taiwan sequence, start 皮 with the long left-falling stroke, then the bent top, vertical, and two lower crossing strokes.

百.note: 百 names the hundreds place. 一百 is one hundred, pronounced yìbǎi in these examples.
百.memory: A single horizontal roof sits above 白. Unlike 白 alone, 百 has that extra top line.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top horizontal
parts.description: Begin with the long horizontal line above the rest of the character.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the slant into the lower 白 and its box with the inner horizontal.

零.note: 零 names zero. Inside a number such as 一百零五, it marks the missing tens place.
零.memory: Rain 雨 sits over 令: keep the rain dots above the pointed lower component.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: rain component
parts.description: Write the rain roof and frame, central vertical, and the four small rain marks.

parts.label: 令
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the two slanting top strokes of 令, then its central mark and lower bent strokes.

千.note: 千 is one thousand, ten times 百. 一千 is pronounced yìqiān.
千.memory: 千 looks like 十 with a short slant added above. Do not mistake it for the straight-topped 干.

parts.label: 丿
parts.name: top slant
parts.description: Start with the short left-falling stroke across the top.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: cross below
parts.description: Write the horizontal and then the vertical crossing through it.

萬.note: 萬 groups ten thousands. 一萬 is 10,000, not 1,000. Use the Traditional form 萬.
萬.memory: The four-stroke grass top covers 禺, whose lower tail reaches down on the right.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: Taiwan grass top
parts.description: The Taiwan glyph writes the grass top with four strokes, as two separated crosses.

parts.label: 禺
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: Write the box and crossing strokes of 禺, then the lower enclosure, hook and final inner mark.

賣.note: 賣 mài, fourth tone, means sell. Compare the earlier 買 mǎi, third tone, meaning buy.
賣.memory: 賣 adds a three-stroke 士 above 買. That extra top distinguishes selling from buying.

parts.label: 士
parts.name: top component
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, vertical and shorter lower horizontal of 士.

parts.label: 罒
parts.name: middle net
parts.description: Write the wide five-stroke net shape in the middle.

parts.label: 貝
parts.name: lower shell component
parts.description: Write 貝 with its stacked box lines and the two short lower strokes.

u13-ask.title: Address the owner, then ask
u13-ask.explanation: 老闆 lǎobǎn is a shop owner or boss. You can use it to address the owner directly. 請問 qǐng wèn politely opens a question: excuse me, may I ask. The actual question still follows it. You already know 多少錢; add 請問 before that question. 請問 is not a greeting or a request to buy something by itself.

examples.text: 老闆，請問這杯茶多少錢？
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, qǐng wèn zhè bēi chá duōshǎo qián?
examples.meaning: Excuse me, how much is this cup of tea? (addressing the shop owner)
Excuse me, how much is it altogether?

u13-ask.remember: 請問 introduces a question. 老闆 addresses the shop owner.

u13-buns.title: Use 個 for buns
u13-buns.explanation: 包子 bāozi is a filled steamed bun. The example here uses a meat-filled bun; the word alone does not specify which meat or guarantee a particular filling. Use the familiar 個 to count them: 一個包子, one bun; 兩個包子, two buns. 子 is neutral-tone zi in this food word. Reuse 要 to order and 吃 to talk about eating.

examples.meaning: How many buns would you like?

u13-buns.remember: Use 個 for the buns and 杯 for the drinks.

u13-help.title: Do something for someone
u13-help.pattern: 請 + 幫 + person + action + object
u13-help.explanation: 幫 bāng introduces the person an action is for. In 請幫我買茶, 請 makes the request polite, 幫我 means for me, and 買茶 gives the action. 微波 wéibō means to microwave; the Taiwan reading has a rising second tone on wéi. To say someone does not do this for you, put 不 before 幫: 他不幫我買茶. The person after 幫 is the beneficiary, not the thing being bought or heated.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ wéibō zhè ge bāozi.
examples.meaning: Please microwave this bun for me.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù bāng wǒ mǎi chá.
examples.meaning: He does not buy tea for me.

u13-help.remember: 幫 + person comes before the action. For a refusal, put 不 before 幫.

u13-hundreds.title: Hundreds and a missing tens place
u13-hundreds.pattern: hundreds + 百 + tens + 十 + ones
u13-hundreds.explanation: 百 bǎi is hundred. 一百 is 100; 一百三十 is 100 + 30 = 130. Keep the internal 十 when there are tens: 一百一十 is 110. 零 líng is zero. If the tens place is missing but the ones place is present, say 零: 一百零五 = 105. Do not add 零 after a complete hundred: 一百 is already 100. Both 二百 and 兩百 can mean 200; these examples use 兩百. We practice full, explicit numbers rather than shortened price readings.

examples.text: 一百、一百一十、一百三十

examples.pinyin: yìbǎi líng wǔ, liǎngbǎi líng bā

u13-hundreds.remember: 105 has no tens, so use 零. 150 has five tens: 一百五十.

u13-large-prices.title: Keep 千 and 萬 apart
u13-large-prices.explanation: 千 qiān means thousand; 萬 wàn means ten thousand. 一千 is 1,000 and 一萬 is 10,000. Read the largest place first: 一萬三千 = 10,000 + 3,000 = 13,000. Add 百 for hundreds: 三千五百 = 3,500. Use 零 once for a gap before a later nonzero place: 一千零五十 = 1,050 and 一千零五 = 1,005. Do not say a 零 for every empty place or add zero at the end. 二千 and 兩千 are both possible; these lessons use 兩千. These are fictional practice amounts.

examples.pinyin: yìqiān líng wǔshí, yìqiān líng wǔ

u13-large-prices.remember: 千 is a thousand; 萬 is ten thousand. A gap before a later value needs one 零.

u13-sell.title: Buy and sell have different tones
u13-sell.pattern: customer + 買 + item; seller + 賣 + item
u13-sell.explanation: 買 mǎi, third tone, is buy: you obtain the item. 賣 mài, fourth tone, is sell: the seller supplies it. 老闆賣包子 means the shop owner sells buns. You can ask 你們賣包子嗎？ or say 你們賣不賣包子？ using the familiar question patterns. With a price, 一個包子賣二十五塊 means one bun sells for NT$25. The practice menu here has buns at 25 each and coffee at 80.

examples.pinyin: Yí ge bāozi mài èrshíwǔ kuài.

u13-sell.remember: 買 mǎi = buy; 賣 mài = sell. Notice both the tone and the extra top of 賣.

u13-ask-price.text: 老闆，請問這杯茶多少錢？
u13-ask-price.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, qǐng wèn zhè bēi chá duōshǎo qián?
u13-ask-price.meaning: Excuse me, how much is this cup of tea? (to the owner)

u13-bun-question.meaning: How many buns would you like?

u13-heat-bun.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ wéibō zhè ge bāozi.
u13-heat-bun.meaning: Please microwave this bun for me.

u13-buy-for-her.pinyin: Qǐng bāng tā mǎi yì bēi chá.
u13-buy-for-her.meaning: Please buy a cup of tea for her.

u13-buy-help.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ mǎi liǎng ge bāozi.
u13-buy-help.meaning: Please buy two buns for me.

u13-snack-order.text: 我要兩個包子和一杯咖啡，外帶。
u13-snack-order.pinyin: Wǒ yào liǎng ge bāozi hé yì bēi kāfēi, wàidài.
u13-snack-order.meaning: I would like two buns and a cup of coffee, to go.
u13-snack-order.note: The practice prices are 25 per bun and 80 for the coffee.
